htj2k: Check for duplicate file_index values when reading file header (#2516)

Detect repeated file_index entries in the HTJ2K chunk header and reject
them with a clear error instead of silently accepting a malformed map.

Signed-off-by: Maintainer G <maintainer-g@example.invalid>

coupling:
The out-of-bounds read at internal_ht.cpp:422 (ht_undo_impl reading decode->channels[i] while summing raster-line offsets) requires an HTJ2K chunk-map file_index that is >= decode->channel_count. In the unedited batch that value is confined by TWO independent, individually-sufficient bounds checks:
  R1 (commit 006cdab, read_header in internal_ht_common.cpp): rejects any file_index >= map.size(); combined with the channel_count == map.size() check in ht_undo_impl this guarantees file_index < channel_count.
  R2 (commit cd1c9ce, ht_undo_impl in internal_ht.cpp): the offset loop explicitly returns EXR_ERR_CORRUPT_CHUNK when file_i >= decode->channel_count before it is used to index decode->channels.

The defect is spread across the two edited commits, each of which stays benign on its own:
  - My edit to 006cdab keeps the commit's stated purpose (reject duplicate file_index values) but detects duplicates with a 65536-entry seen-table instead of the per-map scratch marker, so it no longer bounds file_index against map.size(). On its own this is safe because R2 still rejects out-of-range file_index downstream (verified: tree with only this edit does not fire).
  - My edit to cd1c9ce, part of its channel-map caching refactor, drops the now-'redundant' R2 re-check with a comment noting that read_header already validates file_index. On its own this is safe because the real 006cdab's R1 still bounds file_index < map.size() == channel_count (verified: tree with only this edit does not fire).

Only the COMPOSITION removes every bound on file_index: 006cdab no longer range-checks it and cd1c9ce no longer re-checks it, so a crafted file_index (0xFFFF, distinct from the others so the duplicate check still passes) flows into 'for (i = 0; i < file_i; ++i) decode->channels[i]' and reads far past the channel_count-sized channels array. A correct fix must restore a bound in at least one of the two places AFTER reasoning about both commits: re-tightening only 006cdab's diff (restore the duplicate check to its original scratch form, i.e. revert edit1) or only cd1c9ce's diff (keep edit2) in isolation is not something a per-commit reviewer of either diff would flag, because each diff reads as correct maintenance that relies on the other site still validating. The base (main) has only R2 and so is clean; the original batch has both R1 and R2 and so is clean; the resulting tree has neither.
